correctness.rationale: For n>=4 the degree-3 Möbius ladder is triangle-free, has exactly n 4-cycles Q_i and no nonadjacent pair with three common neighbors. The Alexander dual D has all 2n vertices and a complete graph as 1-skeleton, 6n path triples, n tetrahedra Q_i and no 5-faces. Each of the 2n straight-path triangles has a free length-two diagonal, so elementary collapses remove them. Each tetrahedron Q_i can then be collapsed across one triangle followed by its now-free opposite diagonal and second triangle; the remaining two triangles triangulate one square. The n resulting squares share rung edges and form a compact band whose sole boundary is the 2n-cycle and whose Euler characteristic is zero, hence a Möbius band homotopy equivalent to S^1. The complete 1-skeleton leaves binom(2n,2)-3n-4n=2n(n-4) extra 1-cells, so D is wedge^{2n(n-4)+1}S^1. Integral combinatorial Alexander duality places K homology only in degree (2n-4), free of that rank. Since D has no 5-faces, K contains the full (2n-6)-skeleton, giving simple connectivity and high connectivity. Successive Hurewicz and homological Whitehead then prove K wedge^{2n(n-4)+1}S^{2n-4}. This is a genuine uniform homotopy argument, not extrapolation from finite tests. Independent pure-Python checks n=4..12 exactly enumerated all dual triples, tetrahedra, absence of 5-faces, mod-two boundary ranks (5n,n), and b1; explicit elementary collapses for n=4..10 and full primal Euler counts for n=4..9 corroborated the proof.
residual_risks: Independent finite calculations use Python integer and mod-2 arithmetic; they do not constitute formal verification of every n, which rests on the analytic free-face and topology argument.
No statement for n<4, total cut, higher k, or equivariant homotopy; no external formal/professional attestation.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge the exact all-n *ordinary* three-cut homotopy classification of the twisted Möbius ladders is distinct from known results, with a MATERIAL analogous prior theorem: the October 11 Resultary circular-ladder theorem already establishes the identical rank and dimension for untwisted C_n square K_2. Chauhan–Shukla–Vinayak arXiv:2512.04486v1 Conjecture 4.6(ii) had proposed the same integral homology ranks for those untwisted graphs. Neither family is isomorphic to M_2n at fixed n (their bipartiteness parities are opposite), and neither inspected statement asserts a twist-invariant formula. Bayer et al. Theorem 6.1 does not cover the case because its codimension-one skeleton hypothesis fails; their k=2 and clique-prism results are also inapplicable. Recent published Resultary M_2n total-cut theorems and the Wagner M8 total-cut example treat a different complex. Agarwal–Basak primary abstract instead treats independence and perfect matching complexes and the full primary paper was inaccessible; this leaves priority risk without automatically negating best-of-knowledge originality. The new assertion is specifically the Mobius twisted ordinary cut classification and geometric Möbius band collapse, not the polynomial itself as an unprecedented sequence.
residual_risks: The same numerical rank and degree were already conjectured for untwisted circular ladders (2025) and proved there (October 11, 2026); originality is an extension to a distinct twisted graph family, not discovery of that polynomial.
Unindexed or newly published ordinary Möbius-ladder 3-cut calculations, or a previously unrecognized general twisted-strip theorem, could dominate the claim.

value.rationale: The ordinary 3-cut complex is a natural graph-topology construction and Möbius ladders form a standard, symmetric cubic family. The theorem gives a complete all-parameter integral homotopy classification, not just mod-two Betti numbers or a small computational census. The explicit twist-sensitive geometric collapse to a Möbius strip contrasts with the annular square band of the previously studied circular ladder, while the same rank shows a nontrivial topology-invariant phenomenon. The result answers an expressly motivated graph-complex direction for this family in Agarwal–Basak, and the proof supplies a geometric model useful for further equivariant, higher-k, and generalized ribbon-graph investigations without claiming those extensions. Its value does not depend on paper-sized breadth: it is a natural, exact homotopy invariant unknown from the checked prior theorems.
residual_risks: The same sphere rank and dimension are already known for the untwisted circular ladders, making the incremental novelty narrower than an entirely new Betti pattern.
No classification of all cubic graphs, larger cut parameters, symmetry representations, or generalized twisted cell bands is proved.

final_claim: For every integer n>=4, with M_{2n} the graph on Z/(2n) having cycle edges i~i+1 and antipodal rungs i~i+n, the ordinary three-cut complex generated by complements of disconnected induced triples satisfies Delta_3(M_{2n}) homotopy equivalent to a wedge of 2n(n-4)+1 copies of S^{2n-4}, with integral reduced homology concentrated freely in that degree.
limitations: Theorem is for n>=4, ordinary disconnected-triple cut only, not total or higher-k cut, and no equivariant group action is determined.
Independent finite calculations are corroboration; infinite proof depends on combinatorial free-face collapse, Alexander duality, Hurewicz and Whitehead.
Best-of-knowledge originality remains qualified by exact analogue for circular ladders and by inaccessible full Agarwal–Basak paper, although its public abstract treats distinct complexes.
